edges.why: Item category is a schedule-line determination input.
Item-category billing relevance defines the billing basis.
Item-category assignment can select the item text procedure.
Item-category context can select the relevant incompletion procedure and completeness checks.
Schedule-line control decides whether availability checking and requirements behavior are active.
Ship-to master data can provide the delivering plant.
Ship-to geography is an input to route determination.
Recipient determination consumes partner context.
Plant is an upstream shipping-point input.
Availability is evaluated in the relevant plant and requirements context.
Shipping-point departure geography participates in route determination.
Shipping-point working times and durations participate in scheduling.
Route provides transit and transportation lead-time inputs to scheduling.
Scheduling calculates the material-availability and logistics dates around which the customer promise is evaluated.
Commercial value contributes to credit exposure.
Copy-control pricing type decides copy versus repricing in follow-on documents.
Billing reference creation and data transfer are governed by copy control.
Document texts can become form and output content.
Posted billing documents create output-relevant business objects.
Credit status can prevent process progression depending on configured check and release design.
Missing data recorded by the incompletion control can block creation of follow-on documents depending on the configured status effect.
Missing billing-relevant data can block billing even when the sales document itself can be saved.
Shipping condition is one of the standard shipping-point determination inputs when multiple shipping points are possible.
Shipping condition is an input to sales-order route determination.
A substituted material can change item-category-group context and therefore item behavior.
A substituted material can bring a different delivering-plant default and logistics context.
Product selection can use availability and changes the product whose supply is checked.
The resulting material becomes a pricing input unless copy/substitution rules preserve other semantics.
A material rejected by listing/exclusion does not proceed as a normal accepted sales item.
Free-goods determination creates a subitem whose item category controls free-of-charge behavior.
The free-goods item participates in pricing with free-of-charge semantics.
Tax condition results become part of billing values and tax content.
Tax and billing fields can participate in financial posting and configured account-determination context.
Delivery item category controls whether storage-location determination is required or active.
Delivery item-category settings influence batch processing in delivery execution.
Revenue account determination runs when billing values are transferred to Financial Accounting.
The pricing procedure provides account keys used by revenue account determination.
Item category is a requirements-type determination input when the configured source uses item category plus MRP type.
Requirements type and class are part of the planning control context that influences customer-requirement and availability-check behavior.
